audit.why: EVEN 5.5/10 fits 50.21% over 1908 games: Irelia owns levels 1-5 while Mortal Steel needs two stacks to knock up and Soul Unbound is 22s down, and Yone takes over on crit items.

audit.whatIsWrong: phases[N].why was the generic Irelia template throughout, and spikes[1] called Fate Sealed a 'Mordekaiser-style Ultimate' with a 'knockup-flavored engage', while also saying Vanguard's Edge stuns.
audit.why: Fate Sealed blinks behind the last champion in a line and pulls everyone hit toward him — no knock-up, no realm. Vanguard's Edge damages, Marks and leaves a slowing wall; the stun is Flawless Duet.
audit.corrected: Spikes and phases rewritten to real timings: Soul Unbound 22s at rank 1, Spirit Cleave 14s, Fate Sealed 120s against Vanguard's Edge at 125s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two owner-side errors: whys[0] and early credited Irelia with an 'E slow' and a 'W passive tenacity', neither of which is in her kit. Yone's shield was attributed to his passive.
audit.why: Flawless Duet stuns; Defiant Dance reduces physical damage during the charge and grants no tenacity; the shield is Spirit Cleave (W), scaling with champions hit.
audit.corrected: whys[0] and early rewritten to the real abilities; the Spirit Cleave shield named as the thing your burst has to clear.
sources: enemyKit W text and shield flag

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Soul Unbound 22s to 10s, Spirit Cleave 14s, Fate Sealed 120s.

edits.before: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — your level 1 reset dance already out-trades careless mages.
edits.after: Q the low minions and keep the blade moving — Mortal Steel needs two stacks before the knock-up lands.

edits.before: W joins: the channel shreds incoming damage — hold it for his trade spell, not his autos.
edits.after: W joins: Defiant Dance cuts physical damage — hold it for his empowered Q, not his poke.

edits.before: E completes the engine: the stun into stacked-passive autos is half a health bar at 3. Mid lane rarely budgets for it.
edits.after: E completes the engine: stun into four-stack autos, and Spirit Cleave's shield is only worth what it blocks once.

edits.before: Reset-dance the wave into his face: four stacks, E-stun, Q the kill threat. The lane is a minion-count quiz.
edits.after: Reset-dance the wave into his face: Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1 — commit while his spirit trick is down.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge online — the all-in caps with a wall of disengage-proof marks. Dive with the wave as your fuel.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge online and Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1 — at level 6 your ultimate is the one on the table.

edits.before: First item spike: stacked trades delete mages and your sustain mocks their poke math.
edits.after: First item: his crit ratios and the Spirit Cleave shield out-trade your stacks.

edits.before: Late Irelia surfs the fight: Q-reset through their line, stun the carry pair, and shred whoever peels.
edits.after: Late Fate Sealed pulls your whole side in and his crit deletes you — fight him with your team.

edits.before: His Ultimate coming online at 6 hands him a hard all-in/engage tool that briefly flips the skirmish math.
edits.after: Fate Sealed is 120s at rank 1, so at level 6 your Vanguard's Edge is the ultimate that is actually up.

edits.before: You out-trade with Q resets and E slow before Yone has any Q stacks or passive shield charge.
edits.after: You out-trade with Q resets and the E stun before Mortal Steel has two stacks to knock up.

edits.before: You out-trade Yone from level 1 to 5 because your W passive tenacity and E slow neutralize his Q3 knockup windows, and your Q-E combo punishes his lack of sustain before he has stacks on his passive shield. Keep wave pressure high with Bladesurge resets on minions to zone him off farm and deny the Q stacks he needs to threaten all-ins. Avoid standing still after he's thrown Q1-Q2 through minions since Q3 crit-knockup still one-shots your combo timing if you're careless. Your all-in windows at level 3 and level 5 (E-Q-W) are strictly better than anything he can answer with before his own power spikes in.
edits.after: You out-trade Yone from level 1 to 5 because Defiant Dance cuts the physical damage of his crit autos and Flawless Duet stuns him out of the two-stack Mortal Steel knock-up, and your Bladesurge resets punish a kit with no sustain but the Spirit Cleave shield. Keep wave pressure high with Bladesurge resets on minions to zone him off farm and deny the stacks he needs to threaten all-ins. Avoid standing still once he has thrown one Mortal Steel, since the second one dashes him forward and knocks you airborne. Your all-in windows at level 3 and level 5 are strictly better than anything he can answer with before his own spikes.

edits.before: Q-E-Q into W lets you burst through Yone's early HP pool before his Q3 knockup threat matters; his E mark isn't live long enough at these levels to punish your dash-ins.
edits.after: Q-E-Q into W bursts through Yone's early health before the two-stack Mortal Steel matters; Soul Unbound is 22s at rank 1, so his escape home is down more often than not.

edits.before: Vanguard's Edge stuns and resets off his soul-swap E, but Yone's own Mordekaiser-style Ultimate hits 6 with a knockup-flavored engage that starts winning his all-ins if you're already low.
edits.after: Vanguard's Edge marks everyone it hits and leaves a wall behind them, while Fate Sealed blinks him behind your line and pulls it in — at 125 and 120 seconds, whoever spends first loses the skirmish.

edits.before: - Yone Soul Unbound: matchup-defining — His burst window — survive it and punish the body he snaps back to. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Defiant Dance has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Soul Unbound (E) is 22s at rank 1 and 10s at rank 5 — while his spirit is out, damage he deals is repeated when it snaps back, so punish the body. - Spirit Cleave (W) is 14s and shields him, so force it out before your commit. - Fate Sealed (R) is 120s.

edits.before: Q-reset through two low minions onto his chest, four-stack autos, E-stun the retreat — the wave-funded all-in he budgeted zero for.
edits.after: Defiant Dance reduces physical damage while charging — hold it for his crit auto and the two-stack Mortal Steel, not his poke.

edits.before: Dashing in under-stacked with W down — Irelia without the engine is a melee minion with a famous haircut.
edits.after: Soul Unbound gives him free move speed to sidestep — throw the blades where he must land, not where he stands.

edits.before: Yone spends Soul Unbound early — the closest thing this matchup has to a guarantee.
edits.after: Fate Sealed pulls your team in — answer the blink with Vanguard's Edge wall.

edits.before: Yone wins by landing Soul Unbound, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Yone wins by shielding through your burst with Spirit Cleave, knocking you up on the second Mortal Steel, and out-critting you.

edits.before: Carry through the dance — the wave funds dives no cooldown can, and your R turns skirmishes into no-exit interviews.
edits.after: Carry by killing him before crit: four stacks and a stun beat a 14-second Spirit Cleave shield every time.

edits.before: Ahead, dance louder: crash waves into Yone's face, stun the answers, and surf resets through every river fight.
edits.after: Ahead, keep him under tower: Spirit Cleave shields more per champion hit, so never let him cleave two of you at once.

notes: The content layer credited Irelia with tenacity on W and a slow on E — neither exists in her kit — and attributed Yone's shield to his passive rather than Spirit Cleave (W). Fixed. spikes[1] described Fate Sealed as a Mordekaiser-style ultimate with a knock-up; it is a blink-behind-the-line pull. The mid and late fields still name Trinity/Black Cleaver while report[8] prescribes the Blade of the Ruined King on-hit build; that item disagreement is champion-wide, not matchup-specific, and was left alone.
